extra.message: Insecure Deserialization via pickle.loads — Arbitrary code execution on the server via crafted pickle payload [verified: raw request.body/GET blob is passed directly to pickle.loads with no validation; RCE on any token holder.]

Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Write — Write arbitrary files anywhere the process has permissions, potentially leading to code execution (e.g. overwriting app files, cron, or WSGI config) [verified: name GET param joined onto BASE_EXPORT_DIR with no traversal check, then request.body written via write_bytes; '..' segments escape the directory.]
OS Command Injection in ping probe — Arbitrary OS command execution on the server [verified: host GET param concatenated directly into os.system shell string with no sanitization or shlex.quote.]

Missing matter-scoped authorization on client directory/edit views — Any authenticated attorney or paralegal can read and modify sensitive client PII and conflict-of-interest metadata for clients/matters outside their assignment, breaking the firm's per-matter confidentiality/conflict-wall model. [verified: client_list uses Client.objects.all() unfiltered and client_edit does get_object_or_404(Client, pk=pk) with only a role check (FIRM_ADMIN/ATTORNEY/PARALEGAL), with no can_access_matter/can_modify_matter-style scoping like every Matter/Document view has, letting any attorney/paralegal view and edit any client's PII.]

XXE via unsafe XML parser configuration — Read arbitrary local files, SSRF to internal services, or denial of service via entity expansion [verified: XMLParser configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False on raw request.body enables XXE/SSRF/file read.]

NoSQL Injection via raw MongoDB filter — Bypass query logic, extract unintended records, or execute arbitrary JS via $where operator [verified: payload.get('filter', payload) from raw JSON body passed unmodified to MongoClient find_one with no operator sanitization.]

Hardcoded fallback Django SECRET_KEY — A known SECRET_KEY lets an attacker forge signed session cookies, password-reset tokens, and other cryptographically-signed values (django.core.signing), leading to session forgery/account takeover. [verified: SECRET_KEY hardcoded fallback 'dev-only-change-me' is used whenever DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is unset, a known value that could enable session/CSRF/token forgery.]

DEBUG mode enabled by default with hardcoded fallback SECRET_KEY — Unauthenticated attackers triggering any server error see full tracebacks including source code, local variables, request data, and settings; if the SECRET_KEY fallback is active, sessions/CSRF/password-reset tokens can be forged. [verified: DEBUG defaults to '1' (True) when DJANGO_DEBUG is unset, and SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded known value; no override enforcement exists in settings.py.]

Django DEBUG defaults to True — Unauthenticated attackers who trigger any unhandled exception see full stack traces, source code, local variables, and settings values (including SECRET_KEY and DB credentials), enabling full compromise. [verified: Confirmed same as idx 0 — DEBUG defaults True via os.getenv fallback, exposing stack traces/settings on unhandled exceptions if deployed with unset env var.]

Unauthenticated internal ops endpoint leaks case metadata — Any unauthenticated attacker can query this endpoint and obtain internal case/matter statistics and sensitive summary notes (payment flags, owner contact details) without the X-Internal-Token gate applied to every other ops route. [verified: case_matter_file_048 has no call to _wrk_gate, unlike every sibling endpoint, so it's reachable by anonymous requests and returns internal case metadata.]

Open Redirect — Phishing via redirect to attacker-controlled site, can be used in conjunction with OAuth/token leakage flows [verified: lane GET/POST param passed directly to redirect() with no safe-url/host validation.]

Sensitive data (Authorization header) written to logs — Credential/token exposure to anyone with log access, enabling session/account takeover [verified: logger.warning logs full request body and raw Authorization header verbatim.]

Code Injection via eval() — Arbitrary expression evaluation, potential sandbox escape to code execution [verified: eval() on GET expr with stripped __builtins__ is still bypassable via object introspection (e.g. ().__class__.__base__.__subclasses__()); no other sandboxing.]

CORS misconfiguration with credentialed reflected origin — Any malicious website can make authenticated cross-origin requests and read responses, enabling data theft from the ops API [verified: Origin header reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin alongside Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true.]

Authorization decision trusts client-supplied cookie/header value — Privilege escalation: a caller can set an arbitrary cookie or header to obtain elevated/privileged payroll and casework data that should require a real elevated-role check. [verified: Authorization decision keyed purely on client-supplied cookie/header value ('ops_badge'/'x-ops-badge') with no server-side signature or session binding, though already behind the shared internal-token gate.]

Disabled TLS certificate verification — Man-in-the-middle attackers can intercept/modify traffic to the partner endpoint [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() disables cert verification for the outbound urlopen call.]

Missing secure cookie / HTTPS-enforcement settings — Session/CSRF cookies for privileged legal-case accounts can be captured via network interception (e.g. on an untrusted network or a misconfigured proxy), enabling session hijacking. [verified: settings.py has no SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE, CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE, or SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT settings defined anywhere in the file, leaving Django's insecure defaults (False) in effect.]

CSV formula injection in export_csv — Formula/macro execution or data exfiltration on the machine of whoever opens the exported CSV (typically a firm admin), via a payload planted through ordinary matter/document title fields. [verified: export_csv writes Matter.title, Client.name, Document.title directly via csv.writer with no leading =/+/-/@ sanitization, and these fields are settable by staff via MatterForm/ClientForm/DocumentForm; opening the export in Excel/Sheets can trigger formula execution.]

Information disclosure of internal filesystem path in error response — Reveals internal directory layout aiding further path-traversal or file-write attacks [verified: Same path-disclosure issue as idx 10, confirmed duplicate.]

Security headers explicitly disabled — Removes defense-in-depth browser protections against XSS for responses served from this endpoint [verified: CSP and X-XSS-Protection headers explicitly emptied/disabled for this response path.]

Use of weak PRNG for security-sensitive token generation — Predictable tokens/nonces could be brute-forced or predicted by an attacker who observes prior outputs [verified: random.choice (Mersenne Twister) used to generate a 'code' with no CSPRNG; predictable if used as a security token.]
